newsitem.title: USA: Xerox posts higher profits, though strong dollar hurt.
newsitem.headline: Xerox posts higher profits, though strong dollar hurt.

text.p: Xerox Corp. on Tuesday reported first-quarter profits of $270 million, which exceeded Wall Street expectations for the copier manufacturer, despite a strong dollar that hurt revenues.
The company's net income, equivalent to 78 cents a share, rose from $237 million, or 68 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.
Industry analysts had on average expected the company to post earnings of 70 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst forecasts.

"It was a very strong quarter," said B. Alex Henderson, a Prudential Securities analyst. "These are very good numbers, considering the currency pressure they are feeling." He raised his 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Xerox.
Revenues grew 2 percent to $4 billion from $3.9 billion, Xerox said, although revenues would have grown 5 percent had it not been for the strong dollar.
The company said a drop in paper prices also took a toll on revenues, cutting them by one percentage point.

Company Chairman Paul Allaire predicted the strong U.S. currency, which makes U.S. products more expensive for foreign buyers, would hurt the year's revenues. But he expressed optimism about the Stamford, Conn.-based company's 1997 outlook, pointing to new digital products and cost controls.
"I am optimistic about our outlook," Allaire said in a statement. "The new family of digital copiers we announced last week is better in every respect than conventional ... copiers."
Allaire added that Xerox would announce in two weeks important new digital production publishing and printing products, both black and white and colour.
Digital products contributed 31 percent of first-quarter revenues, an 18 percent increase, reflecting growth in colour copying and printing and in high-speed laser printing and production publishing.

"Although a continued strong dollar will adversely affect our full-year results, we are maintaining our focus on productivity and expense controls in our drive to deliver double-digit earnings growth," Allaire said.

Total U.S. revenues grew 6 percent and revenues from international operations increased 3 percent on a pre-currency basis, reflecting difficult economic conditions in several European countries. Xerox said it saw modest growth in the quarter in Brazil following an exceptional fourth quarter.
The company also said that as part of its ongoing stock repurchase plan, announced in February 1996, it had bought back 8.2 million shares for $406 million as of March 31.
Xerox stock gained 37.5 cents to $57.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
